target_customer: Consumers buying an over-the-counter smartphone-read urine test for UTIs, with telehealth treatment, and later BD as a partner for at-home infectious disease tests
problem: People with suspected urinary tract infections had to visit a clinic or wait for lab results before treatment. Scanwell let them test at home with a dipstick read by a phone camera.
business_model: Consumer test kit plus app, with telehealth prescription partnerships; later white-label app platform for BD

founders.name: Stephen Chen
founders.background_notes: The YC page gives no bio. Third-party profiles disagree on his history and were not used.

competitors.name: Healthy.io (Dip.io)
competitors.what: Smartphone camera reading of a urine dipstick, filed for FDA 510(k) in 2018
competitors.traction_then: Clearance expected by end of 2018, per a 2018 report

technical_complexity.rationale: Computer vision color reading on varied phones and lighting was a solved-but-fiddly problem, and the hard part was FDA clearance of an over-the-counter claim.

defensibility.rationale: FDA clearance was a real barrier, but at least one rival (Healthy.io) pursued the same approach and the product was a dipstick plus an app.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: BD became a partner on its COVID-19 at-home test app and bought Scanwell in December 2021.

market_need_then: UTIs are a common, painful condition that often needs prompt antibiotics, and telehealth was growing. A 2019 report notes several smartphone urine testers had received FDA clearance, which shows demand and regulatory pathway existed.

branding.domain_note: The company's old domain now redirects to an unrelated site, so the site is dead or repurposed.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain health access language on the YC page

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found. The name was functional and the real value was the BD partnership and FDA clearance.

pivots.to: App platform powering BD Veritor At-Home COVID-19 test
pivots.why: COVID-19 created demand for smartphone-read at-home tests; BD said it helped develop the app

outcome_analysis: Scanwell cleared an over-the-counter smartphone UTI test with the FDA, raised a seed round from top funds, and found a bigger role when BD used its app for a COVID-19 at-home test. BD bought it in December 2021 for an undisclosed price that BD called immaterial, so the exit looks like a strategic platform purchase rather than a large venture outcome.
notes: The seed round and investors come from search results of the MobiHealthNews article, whose page returned 403, and the lead investor's own post (page not retrievable) which confirms an announcement; the year 2019 comes from an aggregator and the exact date is unknown. Aggregators also list a $4M seed in 2019, a $1.6M NIH grant and totals from $3.6M to $7.6M, all unverified and not recorded as rounds. Founder education and employers were not found in an opened source. Only one competitor had a dated source.
